summary: Steel fire tower on a Venango County farm, built 1925 and removed 1959 per the register; 1926 newspaper items name its observer.

facts.design: Galvanized steel tower, 65 ft (19.8 m) high; the register calls it a steel Aermotor tower
facts.status_note: The register says it was removed in 1959. No source we read describes what, if anything, remains on the site.

events.note: Newspaper item of September 7, 1925 says the tower was practically complete; the register gives 1925
Byron Blair was manning the tower in April 1926
Byron Blair discovered the first forest fire of the 1926 season in Venango County; about twenty acres burned before it was checked
Coast and Geodetic Survey description places reference mark No. 2 directly beneath the state forest fire tower
The register gives 1959 as the removal year
Registered September 16, 2008, nominated by Henry Isenberg

evidence.quote: This steel Aermotor tower was built in 1925 and removed in 1959.

evidence.supports: 1925 erection on Mrs. Laura Taylor's farm in Victory township, half mile from Springville, eight miles from Franklin, practically complete
evidence.quote: Erection of the new forest fire observation tower located on the farm of Mrs. Laura Taylor in Victory township, one-half mile from Springville and eight miles from Franklin, has practically been completed.

evidence.supports: galvanized steel, 65 feet high, in the woods
evidence.quote: The tower, made of galvanized steel is 65 feet high

evidence.supports: Byron Blair manning the tower; discovered first forest fire of the season in Venango county
evidence.quote: Byron Blair, manning the new Victory fire tower, 10 miles south, discovered the first forest fire Venango county has had this season

evidence.supports: Pennsylvania Railroad men had the blaze under control the same day
evidence.quote: a group of Pennsylvania Railroad men today had the blaze under control

evidence.supports: around twenty acres burned before the flames were checked
evidence.quote: a score of acres were burned before the flames were checked
DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1935

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says steel Aermotor; the 1925-26 newspaper items say galvanized steel. Both can be true. The Aermotor maker appears only in the register.

notes_for_editor: Thin record with two sources. Register and Forest Lookouts page agree on 1925 erection. Only the register gives the 1959 removal year, and the Forest Lookouts page has only a bare 'Removed' label. Newspaper quotes are as reproduced on the Forest Lookouts page (The Derrick, New Castle News); the originals were not read. Height 65 ft converted to 19.8 m. The 1935 NGS description is the latest source and is not a current site record. No access or visit statement exists in either source, so no access or visit facts are recorded. Two WebSearch calls returned nothing tower-specific (Victory Township, Venango County). Not tried: Venango County Historical Society, The Derrick microfilm, Pennsylvania DCNR records.
